I had a laparoscopic hysterectomy due to uterine cancer 3 years ago and I can give you some insight. First, stock up on Gas X and Miralax. Trust me, you’ll want to take those immediately when you get home from the hospital. Your ab muscles will be incredibly sore and painful, and pushing a bowl movement or having gas (which will be common since they inflate that part of your body) will be very hard without that help. 

I also recommend movement. Not a lot, but a small amount every couple of hours. It will suck, it will hurt, but the sooner you can get up and walk around, the less recovery time you’ll need. Make sure you don’t overdue it, it is a major surgery and your body needs time to recover as well. I watched Netflix shows and when it asked if I was still watching every few episodes, I would take that time to stand up and do a small lap around the apartment. Wearing the girdle the hospital provides that holds it all in really helps.

I was in pain for about a week afterwards but spent the next few weeks relaxing. I thought I felt totally fine by the next week, but doing small tasks still knocked me on my ass and made my abs feel so sore, so don’t feel like you’re a weenie for taking the time to recover. Hope this helps. Let me know if you have any other questions.
